They were led by head coach [[Cuonzo Martin]], who was in his first year at Missouri. The team played its home games at [[Mizzou Arena]] in [[Columbia, Missouri]] as sixth-year members of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. On October 22, 2017, the Tigers renewed their rivalry against [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] in an exhibition game for four different charities for [[Hurricane Harvey]] and [[Hurricane Maria]] relief funds. This was the first time the teams had played since [[2010–2014 NCAA conference realignment|Missouri left]] the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] for the SEC.{{cite web|url=http://kuathletics.com/news/2017/10/13/kansas-and-missouri-mens-basketball-come-together-hope-to-raise-1-million-for-disaster-relief-efforts.aspx|title=Kansas and Missouri Men's Basketball Come Together, Hope to Raise $1 Million for Disaster Relief Efforts|website=KUAthletics.com|date=October 13, 2017}} The event raised $1.75 million for hurricane relief.{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21119246/kansas-jayhawks-missouri-tigers-exhibition-game-raises-175-million-hurricane-relief|title=KU-Mizzou game raises $1.75M for storm relief|work=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2017}} They finished the season 20–13, 10–8 in [[2017–18 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fourth place. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2018 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they lost in the second round to [[2017–18 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], where they lost in the first round to [[2017–18 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]]. ==Previous season== The [[2016–17 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 8–24, 2–16 in [[2016–17 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in a tie for 13th place. As the No. 14 seed in the [[2017 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they defeated [[2016–17 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] in the first round before losing in the second round to [[2016–17 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]]. On March 5, 2017, head coach [[Kim Anderson (basketball)|Kim Anderson]] was asked to step down as head coach of the Tigers following the season.{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18830638/coach-kim-anderson-missouri-tigers-part-ways|title=Missouri asks Anderson to step down as coach|work=ESPN.com|access-date=March 6, 2017}} He was allowed to coach the team in the [[2017 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]]. On March 15, the school hired Cuonzo Martin as head coach.{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18915424/cal-cuonzo-martin-resigns-accepts-7-year-deal-missouri|title=Mizzou lures Martin from Cal with 7-year deal|work=ESPN.com|access-date=March 16, 2017}} ==Offseason== Soon after his hiring at Missouri, Cuonzo Martin hired Michael Porter Sr. as an assistant coach.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/michael-porter-jr-commits-to-missouri-after-receiving-release-from-washington/|title=Michael Porter Jr. commits to Missouri after receiving release from Washington|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=October 23, 2017|language=en}} Shortly thereafter, after being released from his commitment to [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] following the firing of Washington head coach Lorenzo Romar, Porter's son, No. 2 overall recruit [[Michael Porter Jr.]], committed to Missouri to play for the 2017–18 season.{{Cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/michael-porter-jr-missouri-washington-commitment-cuonzo-martin-032417|title=Top recruit Michael Porter Jr. commits to Missouri|date=March 24, 2017|work=FOX Sports|access-date=October 23, 2017|language=en-US}} Nearly two months later, his younger brother, [[Jontay Porter]], joined the family to play in Missouri this season. ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
